pages.title: Project Atlas: product overview and current status
pages.author: daniel.pm
pages.body:
Project Atlas overview
Purpose and scope
Project Atlas is Company A's merchant-onboarding workspace for Singapore SME customers.
The target is to reduce median onboarding time from 5 business days to 1 business day; this is a target, not a measured result.
The first pilot covers 10 invited Singapore merchants, document upload, application status and an operations review queue.
Automated approval, overseas merchants and WhatsApp notifications are outside the first pilot scope.
Current status as of 30 October 2026
Atlas is Amber: the pilot is conditional on two remaining callback tests passing and the support SOP being ready.
The revised provisional pilot is 12 November 2026; 6 November 2026 is superseded by decision ADR-003.
Alex Morgan takes product ownership from Daniel Wu on 30 October 2026.
The next go/no-go is 3 November 2026 at 16:00 SGT.
Pointers: ADR-003; ATL-108; ATL-109; Atlas team roster in Drive.

history.body: The initial proposed Atlas pilot date was 6 November 2026; QA sign-off was still pending.

pages.title: Atlas architecture and ownership
pages.author: jdoe
pages.body:
Atlas architecture
Jordan Doe owns the technical design and coordinates the integration.
Samira Khan's merchant status screen calls Elena Park's onboarding API.
The API consumes verification callbacks and writes an application-state event for Mei Tan's funnel dashboard.
A duplicate callback must not move a completed application back to pending.
Priya Raman owns staging, alert routing and the rollback procedure.
The pilot keeps a human operations review before any merchant is approved.
The integration uses a fictional verification sandbox; no real merchant data or live vendor credentials exist in this fixture.

pages.title: Atlas ADR-003: scope and revised pilot decision
pages.author: ava.sponsor
pages.body:
Atlas ADR-003
Decision recorded 29 October 2026
Ava Brooks approved moving the provisional Atlas pilot from 6 November 2026 to 12 November 2026.
The earlier 6 November date is superseded; the revised date remains conditional, not a launch commitment.
Reason: ATL-108 still has two failing callback scenarios and ATL-109 cannot be signed off.
The pilot remains 10 invited Singapore merchants; overseas onboarding is deferred.
Elena Park targets the remaining fix for 2 November 2026; Lucas Reed plans the regression rerun for 3 November 2026.
Alex Morgan must confirm the pilot scope and acceptance criteria with Ava Brooks on 2 November 2026.
Go/no-go owners are Alex Morgan, Lucas Reed, Leo Hartono and Sara Lindqvist; the meeting is 3 November 2026 at 16:00 SGT.
Approval evidence: imported email dated 29 October; confirmation in #proj-atlas.

pages.title: Atlas product-lead handover: first-week checklist
pages.author: daniel.pm
pages.body:
Atlas product-lead handover
Daniel Wu hands Atlas product ownership to Alex Morgan on 30 October 2026.
Step 1: Meet Jordan Doe and Lucas Reed to review ATL-108 and the two failing callback tests on 2 November 2026.
Step 2: Confirm the 10-merchant pilot scope and acceptance criteria with Ava Brooks on 2 November 2026.
Step 3: Review Leo Hartono's support SOP and confirm the pilot exception owner before the 3 November go/no-go.
Step 4: Attend the go/no-go on 3 November 2026 at 16:00 SGT; publish the decision before confirming a pilot date.
Step 5: Check Mei Tan's baseline dashboard before treating the 1-day onboarding goal as an achieved outcome.
Open question: no approved budget figure is recorded in the accessible Atlas project records.

pages.title: Atlas pilot acceptance criteria and rollback
pages.author: lucas.qa
pages.body:
Atlas pilot acceptance criteria
All 120 required regression cases must pass; 118 pass and 2 fail in the 30 October run.
A duplicate callback must preserve the completed application state.
A delayed callback arriving after a retry must not overwrite the newest verified state.
Leo Hartono must publish a support SOP with a named daily exception owner.
Sara Lindqvist must confirm the final pilot access list, using the shareable access checklist.
Priya Raman can disable new pilot invitations and return merchants to the existing operations process if the pilot is stopped.
There is no permission to treat a provisional date as an approved launch.

messages.text: Atlas kickoff: make Singapore merchant onboarding easier to understand and operate. Our goal is 5 business days down to 1; that is a target.
I will own the PRD and handover; Jordan owns technical integration. First pilot is 10 invited merchants.
I will document the API and callback contract before implementation.
Please keep operations review in the pilot; we are not automating approval.
Atlas PRD ready: Singapore merchants, document upload, status screen and operations queue. Proposed pilot date is 6 November, subject to QA.
Scope approved. No overseas onboarding or automated approval in this pilot.
I will test the document-status language before design sign-off.
Atlas research: 4 of 6 synthetic participants could not tell whether documents needed resubmission. Revised copy makes the next required action explicit.
Revised flow received. I will implement upload status and the action-needed state.
These are prototype observations, not a measured production completion-rate improvement.
Atlas frontend and API are integrated in staging. Jordan: API design; Elena: onboarding API; Samira: upload and status screens.
Staging alerts are connected. I will rehearse rollback tomorrow.
Integration complete does not mean ready to pilot. I will run the full 120-case pack.
Atlas QA found 7 failures in the initial 120-case run. They all involve duplicate or delayed verification callbacks. Filed ATL-108.
Reproduced: completed can revert to pending when a duplicate callback arrives. I am adding idempotency checks.
The screen is reflecting the state returned by the API. Changing the label would hide the symptom, not fix it.
Keep the blocker on ATL-108. Do not mark the pilot ready based on a green UI demo.
Atlas status and pilot decision: move the provisional date from 6 November to 12 November 2026. The earlier date is superseded; the new date is conditional on QA and support readiness.
ADR-003 updated. Alex Morgan takes product ownership tomorrow. Handover email and team roster are in Drive.
The pilot remains 10 merchants. I need a named daily exception owner before go/no-go.
QA sign-off remains blocked until all 120 required cases pass.
Atlas current status at 10:00 on 30 October: 118 of 120 required regression cases pass; 2 still fail. Five of the original seven failures are fixed.
I own the remaining callback retry fixes in ATL-108, target 2 November. Please keep that as a target, not a promise.
I will validate alert recipients before the pilot. Rollback rehearsal is complete.
Full rerun on 3 November, then the 16:00 SGT go/no-go. No QA approval yet.
Atlas handover for Alex: team roles and completed contributions are in the Drive team roster. Please ask owners about their current focus.
Alex, start with me for architecture and Elena for the callback fix.
Happy to walk you through the research and why the upload states changed.
I own the event schema and upcoming baseline dashboard; we do not have measured production onboarding time yet.
Atlas support SOP draft is ready; the daily exception owner still needs Alex's confirmation.
I will review it with you on 2 November before confirming pilot readiness.
My shareable access review is complete in ATL-112. We still need the final named pilot-user list.
Use the go/no-go to make the commitment. The 12 November date stays provisional until then.
For my first week on Atlas I will review the callback blocker, confirm pilot scope, settle support ownership and attend go/no-go.
That matches the handover checklist. There is no approved budget figure in these project records; ask Ava rather than assume one.
Confirmed. Bring scope and acceptance questions to our 2 November check-in.

files.content:
Atlas QA run — 30 October 2026, 10:00 SGT
Required cases: 120. Passed: 118. Failed: 2. Pilot QA sign-off: blocked.
Failure A: duplicate callback returns a completed application to pending.
Failure B: delayed callback overwrites a newer verified application state.
Owner: Elena Park for fixes; Lucas Reed for rerun and sign-off.
The two remaining cases are not evidence of lost funds; Atlas is a pre-pilot onboarding workflow.
